concept: Onboarding walks a person through the parts of a screen one at a time the way a printed quick-start card points at an appliance: a full-ink ring is drawn round one part, and a small plastic panel beside it says what the part does, which step this is, and how to go on or stop. CoachMark is that ring and panel for a single part; Onboarding keeps the order and the focus.

default_to_avoid.pattern: onboarding tour that dims the whole page, cuts a spotlight hole round the target and scrolls the page to it
default_to_avoid.why_not: A dimmed page hides the unit the person is learning, the scroll takes the page away from them, and the spotlight is a glow, which P6 keeps for the displays.

default_to_avoid.pattern: coach mark bubble with a pointer arrow, an accent fill and a row of dots as the only step count
default_to_avoid.why_not: An accent fill spends the unit's one orange on a label, the arrow breaks when the bubble flips or shifts, and dots tell the step by shape alone with no number a reader can announce.

references.source: Braun SK 4 radio-phonograph (Dieter Rams, Hans Gugelot, 1956): a printed legend sits beside each part and names it, nothing else on the case moves
Braun quick-start cards of the 1960s: numbered steps printed beside a line drawing, one part marked at a time
Popover in this system: the panel, its placement and its leaving motion are reused by import of the same tokens, with the key replaced by an existing target

derivation.form: The callout is surface.solid plastic with elevation.float and corner.inner on layer.overlay, the same panel Popover and Menu open, and the page behind it is not dimmed.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The count, title and text stand in one column on the panel's inset line, and the keys sit on one row under them.

derivation.consequence: tabular figures everywhere a number changes
derivation.form: The count prints as "2 of 5" in tabular figures at the caption size, so the digits do not shift between steps.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: Back, Next and Skip are the existing 44px keys, so a finger can steer the tour on a phone.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map
derivation.form: Focus moves to the panel when a step opens, Tab runs through Skip, Back and Next, Escape ends the tour, and ending it puts focus back on the part that was marked.

derivation.consequence: no entry choreography, no idle animation; transitions only on state
derivation.form: The panel rises in and sinks out only when the tour opens or ends; moving from one step to the next changes the panel at once, and the page is never scrolled for the person.

derivation.consequence: a relation that is active right now prints at full ink
derivation.form: The ring round the marked part is drawn at full ink with a plain stroke, so the link between panel and part shows without a colour and without orange (P1).

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: The panel, the ring and all three keys are ink on plastic; the tour never takes the orange from the unit's own primary key.

options.name: full-ink ring round the part, "2 of 5" printed on the panel, Skip at the start and Back and Next at the end
a drawn leader line from a node on the part to the panel, with a row of dots as the only count
the count in a recessed window beside the text, the part marked with a dashed outline

variants.reason: A keeps the part visible and marked by a stroke that survives a flip or a shift of the panel, and it prints the count as words a reader can announce; B's leader line crosses the part and breaks when the panel flips (the notch problem Popover rejected) and its dots tell the step by shape alone; C spends the recessed window, which P2 keeps for the one display of a unit, on a counter, and a dashed outline reads as a broken border.

panel.why: The open callout is a plastic body with one short soft shadow on the overlay layer, placed beside the part so no screen edge cuts it, and nothing behind it is dimmed.

ring.why: A full-ink ring with a plain stroke is drawn round the marked part. It never takes pointer events, so the part stays usable under it, and it shows the link in forced colours too.

count.why: The count "2 of 5" is printed in tabular figures in secondary ink at the caption size, so a reader hears the position and the digits hold their place.

title.why: The title is printed in the emphasis size and the medium weight and names the callout for assistive tech through aria-labelledby.

body.why: The text stands under the title on the same inset line in the body size and secondary ink, so the callout reads down one column.

keys.why: Skip, Back and Next share one row of 44px keys under the text, so each keeps its hit area and the row does not move between steps.

skip.why: Skip sits alone at the start of the row, away from Back and Next, so ending the tour is never one slip from going on.

data-side=top.why: When the panel flips above the part it rises from below instead, so it always grows out of the part it describes.

data-state=open.why: Opening the tour is a state change, so it moves. The panel rises in from @starting-style over motion.release on the decelerating curve (D-008), and the ring fades in.

data-state=closing.why: While the tour ends, the panel and the ring fade and the panel sinks back over motion.exit, and no key or reader reaches them (D-008).

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under Reduce motion nothing travels; only a fade remains, on motion.hover, which the tokens keep (D-008).

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the panel keeps a real border and the ring is drawn in the text colour, because shadows are dropped.

transform.why: Opening the tour is a state change, so it moves. The panel rises toward the part (above or below, by data-side) over motion.release on the decelerating curve and leaves over motion.exit on the accelerating one (D-008). Under Reduce motion only the fade stays.

opacity.why: Opening the tour is a state change, so it moves. The panel and the ring fade in over motion.release and leave over motion.exit (D-008). Under Reduce motion only the fade stays, on motion.hover.
